messages:
Dalia: Quick heads-up — ran a host-side profile on a 2k-token decode workload. Seeing unexpected CPU spikes in parsing/tokenization + grpc writev pressure. Perf snapshot pasted below.

Dalia: ```
HOST_PROFILE summary:
  total_ms: 137
  preparse_ms: 28
  tokenize_ms: 42
  kv_lookup_ms: 8
  grpc_writev_ms: 35
  kernel_select_ms: 4
  batching_wait_ms: 12
```

Dalia: Not normal — tokenize is higher than typical and grpc writev is a big chunk of host CPU. Want a quick triage before we push the canary.

Matt: ugh. Did you run with kvcache on? what's the hit-rate?

Dalia: kvcache=enabled. Sampling shows ~92% hit-rate overall but spikes to ~60% during the CPU bursts. Attached flame: https://tiny.red/host-flame (short link).

Kai: can you dump the ingress traces? I suspect smallwrite fragmentation is creating many small writev syscalls.

Priya: also check the kernel selection logs — we've seen cases where the quant path falls back to float kernels due to a shape mismatch and that costs us.

Matt: quick experiment: try forcing kernel_hint=prefer_quant for that model and bump batching heuristic (batch_hint_size 8 -> 12). If we reduce number of small syscalls it might drop grpc_writev_ms.

infra-bot: Canary deploy scheduled: host-preparse-v2 -> 2 pods in us-west2. Will monitor CPU and net.

Dalia: Tried kernel_hint change locally. Tokenizer latency dropped ~30% but grpc writev still high. Command I ran: ```./bin/hostprof --trace ingress --sample 1000 --stack```

Kai: re: writev — when chunk alignment is off the proxy sends several small frames. Try enabling stream_coalesce = true in proxy config (temporary) and re-run.

Matt: Also we need to correlate concurrency patterns — batching heuristics behave very differently for few large requests vs many small concurrent ones.

Dalia: This run had 4-6 large concurrent requests. When concurrency hit ~20, runtime aggregated into jumbo batches and tokenize_ms per-request dropped, but preparse_ms climbed (more CPU per host).

Priya: Action items:
1) Dalia — run kvcache eviction traces during the spike (dump keys and timestamps).
2) Kai — attach nettrace to the canary pods and report writev counts + avg frame size.
3) Matt — test kernel_hint=prefer_quant + batch_hint_size=12 on canary.
4) infra-bot — monitor pod CPU/NET for 2 hours and alert on grpc_writev_ms > 20ms.

Matt: +1. If writev counts stay high we should prototype host-proxy write coalescing (coalesce small writes client-side before send).

Kai: noted. quick reproduce snippet I used: ```python3 perf_runner.py --model redwood-alpha --tokens 2048 --concurrency 6 --profile host```

Dalia: Scheduling the kvcache trace now, will report back in ~25m. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

Matt: Thanks — will keep an eye on the canary.

infra-bot: alert: canary host-preparse-v2 CPU spike detected on pod-17 (90%) — posting raw counters to monitoring channel.
